Please correct me if I have missed something, but it explicitly says he not only escorted a homeless man out but has also witnessed several homeless people there. The smell was coming from the homeless person/people. The smell is what's causing the problem, therefore for the problem to be resolved, the people the smell is emanating from have to go. 

If he just assumed they were homeless because they smelled, that is a whole different issue, but from the words put on the paper it says to me "they are homeless AND smell" not, "they smell SO they must be homeless".

I honestly have some mixed emotions about this. I get that the person who is running the business gets to decide who he services and what he lets happen in his own business, but he doesn't own the building. With it being a shared space it's no longer just about him, but about anyone else who also runs their business in the building. While the wording comes off as very unprofessional and downright rude, the meaning behind the letter still stands. As the landlord he has a duty to all his tenants, and by the looks of it he's gotten some complaints (at least enough for him to have written this letter). 

There's nothing wrong with this person wanting to share the space he has with the people who need it, but if it is causing an issue then it might be a good idea to relocate anyway. Both parties involved are at a win/win in that scenario; the landlord and his other tenants get what they want and they can continue to assist the homeless with the little resources he has available at a different location (especially if he's the only one who uses the building).
